html:
1What You Will Learn

  • How to run A/B tests and iterate safely
  • A diagnosis method for prompt failures, hallucinations and model mismatch
  • Optimization of tokens, latency and cost without losing quality
  • Monitoring in production with logging and observability

2A/B Testing and Iteration

Running case

Lumen Advisory Tests a New Prompt for a Retailer's Returns Assistant

  • Version B of the prompt looks better on five hand-picked examples
  • The client wants it live; Lumen proposes a controlled comparison first

Step Practice
Hypothesis "Prompt B raises policy-correct rate by 3 points without raising cost"
Offline first Run both on the same dataset; reject clear losers cheaply
Online split Randomly split live traffic (or run a shadow mode: B runs silently beside A)
Change one thing One variable per test (prompt, model, retrieval setting) so cause is clear
Metrics Primary metric, guardrail metrics (latency, cost, safety), and a minimum sample size set in advance
Duration Long enough for volume and weekly patterns; do not stop at the first good-looking result
Decision Ship, iterate or revert against pre-agreed thresholds
Rollout Canary a small share, watch, then expand; keep instant rollback
  • Version everything: prompt, model ID, retrieval config, tool set; log the variant on every request.
  • Compare against the current production baseline, not against nothing.
  • Beware of noise: small samples, novelty effects and non-determinism; use repeated runs or confidence intervals for close results.
  • Iterate in small steps; keep a change log of what helped.

3Diagnosing Problems

Symptom Likely layer First check
HTTP errors, timeouts, truncation Integration Status codes, stop_reason, max_tokens, retries
Confident wrong answers after data change Retrieval and indexing Index freshness, retrieved chunks, embeddings
Ignores a rule; inconsistent format Prompt failure Prompt version, instruction clarity, conflicting rules, examples
Invented facts or sources Hallucination Were the facts in the context? Add grounding, quotes, abstain option, verification
Good on easy, poor on hard cases Model mismatch Evals by difficulty; test a stronger tier or effort
Wrong tool or arguments Tool design Descriptions, schemas, number of tools
Slow Latency Prompt length, tier, effort, retrieval depth, no caching
Cost spike Tokens Cache hit rate, prompt growth, loops, model tier

Method

  1. Reproduce with the logged request (prompt version, context, parameters).
  2. Locate the layer by checking what the model actually received (retrieved chunks, tool results) before changing the prompt.
  3. Change one variable, rerun the eval set, compare with the baseline.
  4. Add the failure to the regression set.
Exam tip

Do not rewrite the prompt first. Find where the failure lives (integration, retrieval, prompt, model, tools) using logs and the exact input the model saw.

4Optimizing Tokens, Latency and Cost

Goal Techniques Check
Fewer input tokens Cache stable prefixes; trim context; prune tool results; retrieve fewer, better chunks; compaction Cost per request, cache hit rate
Fewer output tokens Concise-output instructions (sentence limits), schemas, max_tokens as a cap, lower effort Output tokens, truncation rate
Lower latency Streaming, smaller tier, caching, parallel calls, shorter prompts p95, time to first token
Lower cost Routing, batch for non-urgent work (50% off), caching, smaller tier where evals pass Cost per successful task
Higher quality at same cost Better retrieval, examples, structured outputs, validation and retries Eval score
  • Optimize cost per successful task, not cost per call: retries and wrong answers have cost.
  • Never optimize blind: re-run the evals after each optimization; reject a saving that breaks a gated metric.
  • Cascades (cheap first, escalate on low confidence) lower average cost and latency.

5Monitoring in Production

Area Signals Action
Reliability Error and timeout rate, retry rate, 429s Backoff, capacity, fallbacks
Latency p50, p95, time to first token Tune levers (Module 10)
Cost Tokens, cache hit rate, cost per task, spend by workspace Budget alerts, optimization
Quality Sampled judge scores, thumbs, escalations, corrections, citation validity Regression set, prompt fixes
Safety and security Flag rate, refusal rate, injection indicators, tool-denial events Guardrail review
Drift Input distribution, retrieval relevance, model or prompt version changes Re-evaluate; retrain data; update chunks
  • Log the identifiers needed for replay (request id, trace id, prompt and model version, variant).
  • Use dashboards for trends and alerts on thresholds and leading indicators.
  • Keep runbooks: who responds, how to roll back, how to fail over.
Exam tip

Find the layer first (integration, retrieval, prompt, model, tools) from what the model actually received, then change one variable.

Exam tip

A saving that breaks a gated quality metric is rejected: optimize cost per successful task.

6Exam Q&A

S1Prompt B looks better on five hand-picked examples. What should happen before it replaces prompt A?

  • ACompare A and B offline on the same dataset, then run a controlled canary or split with pre-agreed metrics
  • BAsk three colleagues which one they prefer
  • CReplace A immediately because B looked better on the examples and the team is eager to ship the new version
  • DWait until customers complain about A
Show the answer

Answer: A. Controlled comparison on a dataset and live traffic avoids acting on anecdote.

S2What makes an A/B test conclusion trustworthy?

  • AUsing only the cases where B performs best so that the measured improvement looks as large as possible to the sponsor
  • BChanging prompt, model and retrieval together to maximize the gain and then keep whichever mix scored best
  • CStopping the test as soon as variant B leads
  • DOne change per test, a pre-set metric and sample size, guardrail metrics and a baseline comparison
Show the answer

Answer: D. Controlled design and pre-agreed thresholds protect against false wins.

S3A support assistant ignores a formatting rule only on long conversations. Which layer should be checked first?

  • AThe model's weights
  • BThe user's network speed
  • CThe billing configuration
  • DThe exact prompt and context the model received on those requests, including truncation and conflicting instructions
Show the answer

Answer: D. Check what the model actually received before changing anything.

S4An assistant invents a policy number that was never in its context. Which fix addresses the cause?

  • ARemove the system prompt to give the model freedom and rely on its general knowledge to supply the policy number
  • BGround the answer in retrieved sources, require quotes or citations, allow "not found", and verify the numbers
  • CIncrease max_tokens
  • DRaise the temperature to make answers more varied
Show the answer

Answer: B. Grounding in retrieved sources, requiring citations, allowing a not-found answer and verifying numbers reduces unsupported claims.

S5A system is accurate on routine cases but fails on the hardest 8 percent. What does this suggest?

  • AA caching bug
  • BA model-capability mismatch on hard cases; test a stronger tier or higher effort for that slice
  • CA schema mistake
  • DA network failure
Show the answer

Answer: B. Evals by difficulty reveal mismatch; escalate only where needed.

S6Which TWO belong in a production monitoring plan? Select TWO.

  • AAlerts on cache hit rate and p95 latency
  • BMonitoring only average latency
  • CSampled quality scoring with a path to add failures to the regression set
  • DChecking quality only during quarterly reviews
  • ELogging full prompts and customer data indefinitely for convenience
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Leading indicators and quality sampling catch regressions early.

S7A cost-cutting change reduces tokens by 30 percent but the faithfulness metric drops below its gate. What should happen?

  • AHide the metric from the dashboard
  • BReject or rework the change; a saving must not break a gated quality metric
  • CShip it because cost is the priority and the quality metric can be repaired in a later release
  • DLower the faithfulness gate to match
Show the answer

Answer: B. Optimization is accepted only if gated metrics hold.

S8Which rollout approach is safest for a new model version?

  • ACanary a small share of traffic with instant rollback and compare metrics against the baseline
  • BSkip evaluation because the model is newer and the provider has already tested it thoroughly for every customer
  • CRun it only in a developer's browser
  • DSwitch all traffic at once at night, when volume is lowest, and watch the dashboards the next morning
Show the answer

Answer: A. A canary with instant rollback limits the harm of a faulty model version while the metrics are compared with the baseline.

S9Why log the prompt version, model ID and variant on every request?

  • ATo reduce token counts
  • BTo increase the context window so that the model can see earlier prompt versions in the same call
  • CTo avoid needing evals
  • DSo that behavior can be reproduced, compared and attributed to a specific change
Show the answer

Answer: D. Versioned logs make behavior reproducible and let a change in quality be attributed to a specific prompt, model or variant.

S10Latency rose after a release while the model and traffic are unchanged. Which check is most direct?

  • ACompare prompt length and cache hit rate before and after the release
  • BIncrease the rate limit
  • CReinstall the client library on all servers in case a dependency changed during the release
  • DReduce the number of reviewers
Show the answer

Answer: A. A longer prompt or lost cache explains latency and cost shifts.

S11An agent system's failures are hard to reproduce. Which practice helps most?

  • AFull production tracing of decisions and tool calls, with checkpoints so runs can resume
  • BRunning every request twice and averaging
  • CReading individual customer conversations one by one until a pattern in the failures appears
  • DDisabling retries
Show the answer

Answer: A. Full production tracing and checkpoints make non-deterministic multi-step runs diagnosable and resumable after a failure.

S12What is the right unit for cost optimization?

  • ATotal monthly invoice only
  • BCost per successful task, including retries and rework
  • CTokens per second
  • DCost per API call regardless of whether the call succeeded, was retried or was discarded
Show the answer

Answer: B. Failed or repeated attempts are part of the true cost.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
A/B Hypothesis · offline first · one change · pre-set metrics and size · guardrails · canary · rollback
Diagnose Reproduce; find the layer; inspect what the model saw; change one thing; add to regression
Layers Integration · retrieval · prompt · hallucination · model mismatch · tools
Optimize Cache, trim, concise output, route, batch, stream; cost per successful task
Rule A saving that breaks a gated metric is rejected
Monitor Errors, p95, cost, cache hit rate, quality sampling, safety, drift; runbooks
Log Request id, trace id, versions, variant
